analyst.summary: PNB's June-2026 quarter profit jump of over 200% made headlines, but it mostly reflects a weak year-ago quarter (last year's number was cut by a one-time tax charge) rather than a genuine business acceleration - underlying interest income grew only about 2%. The good news is real: bad-loan levels are at a multi-year low (gross bad loans about 2.8% of advances, net bad loans under 0.3%), the bank has set aside provisions covering over 97% of stressed loans, and capital levels are comfortable with no raise needed. The caution is that margins remain below the bank's own target, loan growth is outpacing deposit growth, a chunk of the improved credit costs is aided by recoveries from old written-off loans rather than purely cleaner new lending, and an accounting-rule change due next year will add a real, one-time cost. At the current price versus book value, the stock looks fairly priced for what it can sustainably earn - neither compellingly cheap nor expensive. We rate it Hold.
